test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

The manager said, "When will the report be ready?"

options.text: The manager asked when the report would be ready.
The manager told when report will be ready.
The manager asked if report was ready.
The manager questioned that when the report will be ready.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The manager asked when the report would be ready.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• In interrogative sentences, the reporting verb **"said"** is changed to **"asked"**, "enquired", or "wondered".
 
 
 
• **Connector (Wh- word):**
 
 
• When a direct question begins with a question word (who, which, what, where, **when**, etc.), no conjunction (like 'if' or 'that') is used. The question word itself acts as the connector.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• The modal **"will"** in direct speech is changed to its past form **"would"** in indirect speech because the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• The interrogative form ("will the report be") is converted into the **assertive form** ("the report would be"). The question mark is replaced by a full stop.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager asked when the report would be ready."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses **"told"** (which is not used for questions) and fails to change **"will"** to **"would."**
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it uses **"if,"** which is only used for Yes/No questions, and it changes the meaning/tense significantly ("was ready").
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because **"that"** cannot be used as a conjunction before a Wh- question word in indirect speech, and it fails to change **"will"** to **"would."**
